checks: No eclipse at 1 of 50 covered epochs where the 0.90216 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 219769838 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 0.9022 days. Observations from TESS photometry show the primary eclipse causes a dimming of 0.82%, while a secondary eclipse was detected at 5.0 sigma significance near phase -0.49. The automated detection pipeline achieved a signal-to-noise ratio of 98.1 using the Box Least Squares method, and pixel-level image analysis confirmed the signal with a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise of 15.0, though the centroid offset measured 3.8 arcsec from the target location. This candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. The machine-learning screening score of 0.89 suggests the pipeline's model considers this a likely genuine target, and the candidate passed all data quality checks without flags.
